correctness.rationale: Using the full-text Beck–Janssen–Jochemko Theorem 1.8 classification, a width-one member lies in an integer-normal slab of width ≤1 and has Euclidean inradius ≤1/2. The unique exceptional GL(3,Z) class has edge determinant ±4; half-cofactor W has integral columns, |det W|=2, and even column sum. Opposite facet pairs have widths 2/||w_i||, giving r=1/max_i||w_i||. Integral determinant excludes three norm-one columns, hence max norm≥√2. Explicit unimodular V* attains √2 cofactor norms. If equality holds, at most norm√2 columns and parity excludes any norm-one column; the three norm-two vectors must have distinct zero positions, off-diagonal pairings ±1, product +1 and W Gram I+J up to signs. Cofactor inversion gives V Gram 4I−J; all maximizers are Euclidean congruent. All 6 facets tangent and 3 independent opposite planes force unique incenter. No finite experiment is promoted to proof of the general theorem.
residual_risks: The proof relies on cited nontrivial complete lattice-equivalence classification, which was directly inspected, not reproved here.
Finite bounded normal enumeration and m=0..4 Ehrhart counts corroborate, not replace, the universal symbolic argument.

value.rationale: Ehrhart h*-degree exactly two is a natural whole class with a sharp published lattice-equivalence classification. The Euclidean inradius is not invariant under GL(3,Z), so determining its global maximum and the unique metric equality shape among infinitely many lattice representatives is a distinct geometric problem. The width-one versus exceptional strict gap and six-facet tangency classify a natural exact metric invariant. The argument uses a motivated arithmetic cofactor/parity rigidity lemma; it is not a known numeric-table recomputation, arbitrary slice, or mere coordinate substitution.

Potential earlier equivalent metric rigidity could reduce incremental value if found; not present in actual inspected sources.
